top_line: A Houthi missile strike on Riyadh's main airport killed 12 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest attack in a Gulf Arab state since the Iran war began. Trump announced an 'energy ceasefire' in Ukraine that Kyiv called news to it and Moscow has not confirmed, while Washington presses Kyiv to stop striking Russian refineries.

stories.headline: Houthi missile strike on Riyadh's main airport kills 12 and wounds more than 300
stories.what_happened: Saudi authorities say a missile attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday killed 12 people and wounded more than 300; the Houthis claimed the attacks. A second strike on Sunday hit a passenger terminal, killing a Pakistani national and injuring 11. The NYT calls Saturday's strike the deadliest attack in a Gulf Arab country since the US–Israeli war with Iran began in February.
stories.why_it_matters: The war in Yemen is now reaching the Saudi capital's main airport, not just border cities, and governments including the US, Australia, Canada, Japan, South Korea and New Zealand now advise against travel to the kingdom. The Guardian's analysis argues it undermines the US approach of 'parking' the Iran and Yemen wars, while Iran has offered to facilitate Saudi–Houthi talks.

whats_new.before: Houthi strikes on Abha and Riyadh airports had killed three people as the Saudi-backed offensive in Yemen continued.
whats_new.now: A far deadlier strike hit Riyadh, a second followed a day later, Western and Asian governments issued travel warnings, and Iran has offered to mediate.

stories.headline: Trump announces an 'energy ceasefire' in Ukraine that Kyiv calls news to it and Moscow has not confirmed
stories.what_happened: Trump said on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to stop targeting refineries, power plants and other energy infrastructure, without giving details. Zelenskyy said the announcement was 'news to me' but that Ukraine would support such a truce if Moscow does, and reported fresh Russian strikes on power facilities in Kyiv and Kharkiv; the Kremlin has not confirmed any deal. It follows a US deal to temporarily lift sanctions on imports of Russian diesel, and an FT report that the US threatened to block arms for Ukraine unless Kyiv stops striking Russian refineries.
stories.why_it_matters: The US is now openly pressing Ukraine to stop its campaign against Russian oil refineries, a central part of its strategy, as fuel prices rise ahead of the midterm elections. That is opening a rift between Washington and Kyiv's European backers, who publicly rallied behind Zelenskyy after Trump called for a new Ukrainian leader. Oil prices fell on the announcement.

whats_new.before: Russia was striking Ukraine's energy grid and Ukraine was hitting Russian refineries, with no ceasefire in sight.
whats_new.now: Trump has announced a partial energy truce without visible agreement from either side, backed by pressure on Kyiv and a diesel deal with Moscow that lawmakers from both US parties criticise.

stories.headline: At least 139 migrants die as a boat from Djibouti to Yemen capsizes
stories.what_happened: At least 139 people, including 15 children, died and 84 are missing after an overcrowded boat capsized off Obock in Djibouti on the night of 8–9 October, the UN migration agency IOM said. The boat was carrying 305 people, most of them Ethiopian, toward Yemen.
stories.why_it_matters: The IOM says this is among the deadliest shipwrecks ever recorded on the route from the Horn of Africa to Yemen. People are still making the crossing even as war escalates in Yemen and fighting continues in northern Ethiopia.

stories.headline: El Niño breaks a temperature record in a key Pacific zone before its expected peak
stories.what_happened: Temperatures in a key Pacific monitoring zone have set a record for El Niño, the EU's climate monitor said, before the episode's expected peak later this year. Forecasters have warned for months that this El Niño could become the strongest ever observed. Separately, NASA says Antarctic sea ice reached its third-lowest winter maximum on record.
stories.why_it_matters: A record El Niño on top of long-term warming raises the odds of extreme heat, drought, fires and floods in many regions over the coming months. Its effects are already being linked to fires on Borneo and Sumatra, which have made Singapore the world's most polluted city on IQAir's ranking.

whats_new.before: Forecasters expected a very strong El Niño on top of record ocean heat.
whats_new.now: A temperature record has been set before the peak, and Antarctic sea ice reached one of its lowest maxima.

stories.headline: EU and China agree to halve Chinese hybrid car shipments to Europe, as Paris pushes 'Made in Europe'
stories.what_happened: The EU and China reached an 'understanding' on Friday that would cut China's shipments of hybrid vehicles to Europe by half, according to Semafor and the FT. Carmakers welcomed it, while other industries warned China's trade surplus will persist without further action. Volkswagen's chief backed EU 'Made in Europe' rules, and Macron is using the Paris Motor Show to push for state aid tied to EU production.
stories.why_it_matters: It is the first concrete result of this month's tense EU–China talks, and it protects one sector rather than the wider trade balance. Pressure for 'European preference' rules suggests Brussels may keep moving toward industrial protection.

whats_new.before: EU–China trade talks opened in Beijing as France and Germany called for a fast trade weapon against imports.
whats_new.now: A sector deal on hybrids has been reached; other industries want more.

stories.headline: Youth-led protests over India's voter-roll revision lead to thousands of detentions

stories.headline: Poland warns NATO to prepare for a deadly Russian 'hybrid' attack
stories.what_happened: Poland's foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, said NATO should prepare for a deadly Russian 'hybrid' attack, saying the risk of casualties is rising as Moscow escalates sabotage in Europe. The FT reports spy agencies warning that Russia has stepped up efforts to kill European defence chiefs, and companies are increasing security for executives. Separately, Polish police detained a man suspected of planning to assassinate Prime Minister Tusk and his defence minister; no motive has been reported.

stories.headline: Housing protests in Portugal: dozens camp in Porto as the PCP proposes a housing package
stories.what_happened: Protesters took to the streets in Portugal over rising living costs and housing prices. In Porto, more than 50 people have camped out for the right to housing and dozens of tents remain. The Communist Party (PCP) has presented a housing package with new rules on land and public property.
stories.why_it_matters: Protests add political pressure as the Government's rental-law liberalisation goes through parliament, and as the housing movement in Spain grows.

whats_new.before: Parliament approved the Government's rental law in a first vote, and the Bank of Portugal governor said the housing response lacked urgency.
whats_new.now: Street protests and an encampment in Porto, and opposition proposals on land and public property.

stories.headline: Young buyers in Portugal may pay less property tax in 2027, as Catalonia adds an asbestos certificate for sales and rentals
stories.what_happened: The Portugal News reports young homebuyers may save on property taxes in 2027. Cantanhede has kept its IMI and other municipal tax rates for 2027. In Spain, Catalonia is adding a new certificate requiring sellers and landlords to show whether a property contains asbestos.
stories.why_it_matters: Tax relief for young buyers and municipal IMI decisions affect purchase costs in Portugal, and Catalonia's certificate adds a new compliance step for property transactions there.

whats_new.before: No 2027 property-tax changes for young buyers had been reported.
whats_new.now: Further tax savings for 2027 are reported, and Catalonia is adding an asbestos requirement.

signals.title: US fuel-price politics is reshaping two wars
signals.what: Ahead of the midterms, Washington lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, pressed Kyiv to stop striking refineries and announced an energy truce. Meanwhile the Houthis carried out their deadliest strike yet on Riyadh, undermining the plan to 'park' the Gulf conflicts.
signals.why_it_matters: US policy on Ukraine and the Gulf is increasingly driven by energy prices at home, which strains relations with Kyiv and Europe without halting attacks on energy and transport.
signals.would_confirm: A confirmed and observed energy truce, a US arms pause for Ukraine, or more sanctions relief tied to fuel.
signals.would_invalidate: Russia rejecting the truce and the US resuming support without conditions.

signals.title: Digital infrastructure is becoming a front line
signals.what: Data centres are being struck in war, contested in elections and financed through lease commitments that lenders are now scrutinising.
signals.why_it_matters: Physical, political and financial risks to data centres could slow the AI build-out or push it to new locations.
signals.would_confirm: More strikes on data centres, new local moratoriums, or wider credit spreads for data centre borrowers.
signals.would_invalidate: Strikes stop under the energy truce and opposition fades after the midterms.

signals.title: Housing protest spreads from Spain to Portugal
signals.what: After Spain's housing movement helped trigger a snap election and a general-strike call, Portugal is seeing street protests and a housing encampment in Porto as rents there rise far faster than purchase prices.
signals.why_it_matters: Political pressure could shape Portugal's rental-law liberalisation and the EU Housing Act.
signals.would_confirm: Larger or repeated protests in Portuguese cities, or changes to the rental law before the final vote.
signals.would_invalidate: Protests stay small and the rental law passes unchanged.

watchlist.why: Confirmation, or continued strikes on power plants, will show whether the truce exists.

watchlist.item: Saudi response to the Riyadh airport strikes
